arxiv-2111-14667.title: Off-equilibrium non-Gaussian fluctuations near the QCD critical point: an effective field theory perspective
arxiv-2111-14667.creator: Noriyuki Sogabe, and Yi Yin
arxiv-2111-14667.description: Abstract The non-Gaussian fluctuations of baryon density are sensitive to the presence of the conjectured QCD critical point. Their observational consequences are crucial for the ongoing experimental search for this critical point through the beam energy scan program at Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC).

arxiv-2202-09341.title: Perfect sampling of stochastic matching models with reneging
arxiv-2202-09341.creator: Thomas Masanet, Pascal Moyal
arxiv-2202-09341.description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce a slight variation of the Dominated Coupling From the Past algorithm (DCFTP) of Kendall, for bounded Markov chains. It is based on the control of a (typically non-monotonic) stochastic recursion by a (typically monotonic) one.

arxiv-2206-01640.title: PROMISSING: Pruning Missing Values in Neural Networks
arxiv-2206-01640.creator: Seyed Mostafa Kia, Nastaran Mohammadian Rad, Daniel van Opstal, Bart van Schie, Andre F. Marquand, Josien Pluim, Wiepke Cahn & Hugo G. Schnack
arxiv-2206-01640.description: Abstract While data are the primary fuel for machine learning models, they often suffer from missing values, especially when collected in real-world scenarios. However, many off-the-shelf machine learning models, including artificial neural network models, are unable to handle these missing values directly. Therefore, extra data preprocessing and curation steps, such as data imputation, are inevitable before learning and prediction processes.

arxiv-2212-10779.title: Minimum Phase Linear Antenna Array Design
arxiv-2212-10779.creator: J.C. Olivier, E. Barnard
arxiv-2212-10779.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by J.C. Olivier, E. Barnard. The paper considers the design of minimum phase discrete linear arrays. The paper introduces recent advances for the design of minimum phase Finite Impulse Response filters, as applied to the design of minimum phase linear arrays. The minimum phase linear array is demonstrated to require the least number of elements of all linear arrays that are able to achieve a given magnitude pattern specification. Three example designs are presented and compared to results from the literature.

arxiv-2405-20125.title: Haloes, other dark matter candidates and astrophysical implications
arxiv-2405-20125.creator: Philippa S. Cole
arxiv-2405-20125.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Philippa S. Cole. It is possible that a multi-component dark matter model is required if primordial black holes only contribute to a fraction of the energy density in dark matter. This is increasingly more likely with respect to the case of f PBH = 1 f_{\rm PBH}=1 , since there is only one remaining window, on asteroid-mass scales, where primordial black holes can make up all of the dark matter.

arxiv-2410-21380.title: Inverse Faraday effect in disordered two-dimensional electronic systems
arxiv-2410-21380.creator: Maxim Dzero
arxiv-2410-21380.description: Abstract I formulate a theory of the inverse Faraday effect in impure two-dimensional metallic system with lifted spin degeneracy induced by Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Using the formalism of non-equilibrium quantum field theory, the static contributions to the current density up to the second order in powers of external electromagnetic field are evaluated.

arxiv-2506-17190.title: Comparison of spin-qubit architectures for quantum error-correcting codes
arxiv-2506-17190.creator: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, Chien-Yuan Chang
arxiv-2506-17190.description: Abstract We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-electron Zeeman qubits (Loss–DiVincenzo qubits), and a hybrid approach combining Zeeman and singlet-triplet qubits.

pmc-10644230.title: Case report: Clinical management of recurrent small cell lung cancer transformation complicated with lung cancer-induced acute pancreatitis after lung adenocarcinoma surgery
pmc-10644230.creator: Suyun Zhang, Ningjing Guo, Qianyuan Zhang, Yao Wang, Sheng Yang, Xiangqi Chen
pmc-10644230.description: In the diagnosis and treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the histological type may change from lung adenocarcinoma to lung squamous cell cancer or small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Pancreatic metastasis is extremely rare in advanced lung cancer, and pancreatitis characterized by lung cancer metastasis-induced acute pancreatitis (MIAP) is more rare.

pmc-10713776.title: In vivo CRISPR/LbCas12a-mediated knock-in and knock-out in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar L.)
pmc-10713776.creator: Mari Raudstein, Erik Kjærner-Semb, Morten Barvik, Silje Broll, Anne Hege Straume, Rolf Brudvik Edvardsen
pmc-10713776.description: Genome editing using the CRISPR/Cas system offers the potential to enhance current breeding programs and introduce desirable genetic traits, including disease resistance, in salmon aquaculture. Several nucleases are available using this system, displaying differences regarding structure, cleavage, and PAM requirement. Cas9 is well established in Atlantic salmon, but Cas12a has yet to be tested in vivo in this species.

pmc-12542851.title: Effects of Melatonin Disorders on Parkinson’s Disease: A Review of Mechanisms and Clinical Manifestations
pmc-12542851.creator: Yiwei Shen, Cong He, Yulin Wang, Yu Zhang, Zhengnan Liu, Xia Chen, Shun Wang, Yan Bai
pmc-12542851.description: Melatonin is a vital hormone that is important for antioxidant activity, neuroprotection, and biological rhythm control. Melatonin anomalies may have a high correlation with the onset and development of Parkinson’s disease, according to recent studies. A common neurodegenerative illness that severely lowers a patient’s quality of life, Parkinson’s disease is typified by non-motor symptoms and aberrant movement.

pmc-12770517.title: Backpropagation through space, time and the brain
pmc-12770517.creator: Benjamin Ellenberger, Paul Haider, Federico Benitez, Jakob Jordan, Kevin Max, Ismael Jaras, Laura Kriener, Mihai A Petrovici
pmc-12770517.description: How physical neuronal networks, bound by spatio-temporal locality constraints, can perform efficient credit assignment, remains an intriguing question. Both backward- and forward-propagation algorithms rely on assumptions that violate this locality in various ways. We introduce Generalized Latent Equilibrium (GLE), a framework for fully local spatio-temporal credit assignment in physical, dynamical neuronal networks.

pmc-13641678.title: Steatotic liver disease spectrum: From MASLD to MetALD and beyond - Clinical outcomes and precision medicine frontiers
pmc-13641678.creator: Won Kim
pmc-13641678.description: r disease (SLD), the new nomenclature formally acknowledged a clinical reality that hepatologists have long recognized at the bedside: metabolic dysfunction and alcohol exposure frequently coexist in the same patient, interact synergistically, and shape prognosis along a continuous, and modifiable, spectrum rather than within mutually exclusive diagnostic silos.

pmc-13656379.title: Patient-specific variables predicting triage outcomes of ear, nose, throat referrals from primary care for dysphonia
pmc-13656379.creator: Christopher Payten, Duy Duong Nguyen, Kelly Weir, Catherine Madill
pmc-13656379.description: BackgroundPatients with dysphonia are referred to Speech-Language Pathologists (SLP) or Ear Nose and Throat (ENT) surgeons from General Practitioners (GPs) for specialist assessment. Accurate referral information is needed to determine the assessment-pathway and priority. This study aimed to examine which patient-specific information provided in GP referral documents predicted clinicians' triage outcomes.
